issue.body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->
on Zsh, battery percentage character print `%{`.
this PR fix print `%{` -> `%`.

#### Description
on Zsh, `%` is prompt sequence prefix.
http://zsh.sourceforge.net/Doc/Release/Prompt-Expansion.html

i.e,
`%n` will print username,
`%%` will print `%`, etc.

this problem on only Zsh. Bash and Fish are print `%`.
So, switch percentage character by `STARSHIP_SHELL`.

<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

repository.description: ☄🌌️  The minimal, blazing-fast, and infinitely customizable prompt for any shell!

issue.body:
## Why refactor Starship?

The Starship team wishes to refactor the Starship codebase. The following reasons explain why:

- The complexity of the codebase has grown considerably since its inception
- Making per-shell tweaks easier to do as support for more shells increases
- Building a more robust and testable codebase
- Allowing for safer and more [granular configuration](https://github.com/starship/starship/issues/132#issuecomment-520172694)
- The project will be architected in a way that better follows Rust conventions

Refactoring plans will be managed in this GitHub project: https://github.com/starship/starship/projects/2

## What to refactor in Starship?

### Initialization

The current two-layer approach to initializing has occasionally been brittle given how complex it is. It may be best to rethink our approach to initializing, possibly bringing it back to a single initialization script.

Another thing to think over is how we could potentially remove the shell argument from the script, making it automatically detect the shell being used.

This would also be a good opportunity to consider using environment variables rather than flags for passing in values from shells.

### Prompt Configuration

This presents a good opportunity to make our configuration more robust, using enums over strings (#132).

We could also use this opportunity to prepare for more complex modules, allowing for per-segment configuration, as proposed here: https://github.com/starship/starship/issues/132#issuecomment-520172694

We would also be implementing error handling and surfacing configuration errors as part of the prompt if unexpected options or values are used.

### Module Architecture

Modules are currently dependant on shared global initialization of values in Context, even if they are unused. We could instead lazily assign these values in Context to avoid setting them if the modules they're in are unused.

We could begin experimenting with caching external command outputs based on the date created or size of the binaries we execute, allowing for modules that would traditionally be slower.

### Printing Process

The current printing process assumes that the text representation of the module is the form that can be emitted. Unfortunately, it turns out that various shells interpret different characters differently and need different representations to be emitted (see #110, #226, and [elvish](https://github.com/elves/elvish) for examples of where this breaks).

It seems the best way to handle this is to create a layered system: instead of outputting modules directly into printable text, we instead create an internal representation, and then choose how to render them. The "rendering" could be done with ANSI color codes, a terminal-specific method, or even JSON.

Steps:
  - [ ] Create internal representation for modules
  - [ ] Create way to pass starship information to renderer
  - [ ] Write rendering modules for various outputs (e.g. ANSI term, elvish prompt syntax)

One thing to note is that our current color management system, ANSI-term, will probably not be good for an internal representation. One package to potentially look into for this would be [pastel](https://github.com/sharkdp/pastel), from sharkdp (the creator of `bat` and `fd`)
